title: An injective extension recurrence corrects horseshoe defects
statement:
Let C be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], S and T short exact sequences in C,
and F a morphism from S to T. Let IA, IB, IC and JA, JB, JC be injective resolutions
[def-sp-injective-resolutions] of the three terms of S and T respectively. Let
alpha, beta and alpha', beta' be chain maps between the corresponding resolutions,
with zero composites, with short exact rows in every nonnegative degree, and with
all four augmentation squares commuting. Let phiA and phiC be prescribed chain maps
between the first and third resolutions respectively, lifting the first and third
components of F. Let t be a family of maps from IB in degree n to JB in degree n,
commuting with both outer row squares in every degree. Then there is a family k from IC in degree n to JA in degree n such that
subtracting beta followed by k followed by alpha' from t commutes with the two
complex differentials in every degree and, in degree zero, lifts the middle component
of F on the augmentation. No outer square for the corrected family is asserted here.

proof.text: Obtain E and e, their two defect factorizations, their augmentation compatibility, and their signed cocycle identity.

Extend e across the monic augmentation of IC into the injective degree-zero term of JA, giving k0. Exactness at the augmentation and injectivity of JA in degree one descend k0 dA minus E0 along dC, giving k1.

Given consecutive k values, the cocycle identity and square-zero differentials show that k-next dA minus E-next vanishes on the preceding dC. Use exact_succ.descToInjective to descend it along the next differential. Dependent Nat recursion supplies all k, with the required primitive identities.

Distribute composition over subtraction, use the two chain-map identities for alpha' and beta, and substitute the primitive equations. The E factorization cancels the differential defect and the e factorization cancels the augmentation defect.

theorem horseshoe_homotopy_correction
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [Abelian C]
    (S T : ShortComplex C) (hS : S.ShortExact) (hT : T.ShortExact) (F : S ⟶ T)
    (IA : InjectiveResolution S.X₁) (IB : InjectiveResolution S.X₂)
    (IC : InjectiveResolution S.X₃) (JA : InjectiveResolution T.X₁)
    (JB : InjectiveResolution T.X₂) (JC : InjectiveResolution T.X₃)
    (α : IA.cocomplex ⟶ IB.cocomplex) (β : IB.cocomplex ⟶ IC.cocomplex)
    (α' : JA.cocomplex ⟶ JB.cocomplex) (β' : JB.cocomplex ⟶ JC.cocomplex)
    (hαβ : α ≫ β = 0) (hαβ' : α' ≫ β' = 0)
    (hα : IA.ι ≫ α = (CochainComplex.single₀ C).map S.f ≫ IB.ι)
    (hβ : IB.ι ≫ β = (CochainComplex.single₀ C).map S.g ≫ IC.ι)
    (hα' : JA.ι ≫ α' = (CochainComplex.single₀ C).map T.f ≫ JB.ι)
    (hβ' : JB.ι ≫ β' = (CochainComplex.single₀ C).map T.g ≫ JC.ι)
    (hexact : ∀ n : ℕ, ((ShortComplex.mk α β hαβ).map
      (HomologicalComplex.eval C (ComplexShape.up ℕ) n)).ShortExact)
    (hexact' : ∀ n : ℕ, ((ShortComplex.mk α' β' hαβ').map
      (HomologicalComplex.eval C (ComplexShape.up ℕ) n)).ShortExact)
    (φA : IA.cocomplex ⟶ JA.cocomplex) (φC : IC.cocomplex ⟶ JC.cocomplex)
    (hφA : IA.ι ≫ φA = (CochainComplex.single₀ C).map F.τ₁ ≫ JA.ι)
    (hφC : IC.ι ≫ φC = (CochainComplex.single₀ C).map F.τ₃ ≫ JC.ι)
    (t : ∀ n, IB.cocomplex.X n ⟶ JB.cocomplex.X n)
    (htα : ∀ n, α.f n ≫ t n = φA.f n ≫ α'.f n)
    (htβ : ∀ n, t n ≫ β'.f n = β.f n ≫ φC.f n) :
    ∃ k : ∀ n, IC.cocomplex.X n ⟶ JA.cocomplex.X n,
      (∀ n,
        (t n - β.f n ≫ k n ≫ α'.f n) ≫ JB.cocomplex.d n (n + 1) =
          IB.cocomplex.d n (n + 1) ≫
            (t (n + 1) - β.f (n + 1) ≫ k (n + 1) ≫ α'.f (n + 1))) ∧
      IB.ι.f 0 ≫ (t 0 - β.f 0 ≫ k 0 ≫ α'.f 0) =
        ((CochainComplex.single₀ C).map F.τ₂ ≫ JB.ι).f 0
